newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices ease, no impact from INRO.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices ease, no impact from INRO.

text.p: Thai rubber prices continued heading down this week in a listless market with only Japan buyers featured, traders said on Friday.
News that the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) was set to resume intervening in the market barely had any affect on the market.
"I wouldn't be too excited, at least not now. Even though the market is very bearish, we are still about $200 per tonne away from the intervention level," said a Bangkok-based trader.
But government officials welcomed the move, saying any INRO intervention would help reduce pressure for the government to support local producers.
Thailand promised to carry out the price intervention scheme in the domestic market from May until the end of July. However, the program can be extended if global prices remained weak.
A senior Thai official told Reuters in London that the government planned to buy up to 100,000 tonnes of unsmoked sheet rubber under the scheme.
"It is a good news even though there is no immediate impact right now," the official said.
In the market, trade was subdued by bearish demand, traders said. There were inquiries from European clients, but no actual buying was heard.
"It's really dull out there. The prices are likely to drop further next week," said another trader.
"With the market like this, buyers expect prices to drop further. So, they stay on the sidelines. Bids were quite low compared to offers," he said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for August delivery was quoted around 112.00 US cents per kg FOB Bangkok from 112.50 previously. September was quoted around 112.50 US cents per kg on the same basis.
